Subject: Post-call: Migration & compatibility evaluation (OpenAI API compatibility / SDK swap)

Thanks for the time today, Evan — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recap: we walked through Redwood's hosted & private deployment options and discussed your migration goals (minimize code changes, maintain prompt behavior, and avoid regressions vs your current OpenAI setup). You flagged two main concerns: API parity (function calling, streaming), and prompt diffs across model variants.

- Differentiators to watch for in this eval: 1) OpenAI-compatible API endpoint for drop-in SDK swaps; 2) predictable latency under your seq-length & concurrency patterns (we'll run a latency/cost baseline); 3) transparent model mapping & fallbacks so prompts behave consistently across variants.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint + quick SDK swap guide (Python/Node) so your engs can run a smoke test. Attachment: redwood-compat-checklist.pdf and openai-shim-guide.md.
2) Aditya (SE) will share benchmark scripts you can run against your typical prompts to capture latency/cost differences. Attachment: benchmark-scripts.zip.
3) We’ll propose a 1-week POC window (suggested: Mar 2–6) for you to run integration tests and prompt diffs; we’ll iterate on any prompt/response mismatches.

Would you like us to schedule a 30–45m technical kickoff with your eng lead + Aditya next week to walk through the setup?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Smoke test: can you confirm whether the OpenAI-compatible endpoint supports both streaming responses and function-calling semantics the same way OpenAI does? A lot of our stack relies on function_call for structured outputs.
- SDK swap: our backend uses the OpenAI Python client (v1). If we can swap endpoint + a small config change we can validate quickly. Any example diffs you can share would be great.
- Prompt diffs: we’ll run a small set of 20 representative prompts (mix of few-shot and system-level) — what’s the best way to surface response deltas to you?

Looping in procurement (procurement@finco.com) for visibility — they’ll want a procurement/process contact if the POC looks good.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Migration & compatibility evaluation (OpenAI API compatibility / SDK swap)

Great — answers inline and proposed concrete items.

1) Function calling & streaming: yes. We expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint supporting streaming (chunked responses) and the function_call field. There are a few runtime nuances (see note below), but the API surface and payloads match OpenAI’s so your current client code will largely be unchanged.

2) SDK swap: attached openai-shim-guide.md contains copy-paste snippets for Python and Node (example: set REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL, and point the client to our /v1 endpoint). Minimal changes expected — usually a single-line client config change and optionally updating model name.

3) Prompt diffs: please drop your prompt set (20 examples) in the shared Drive folder (link in related links). We’ll run compare reports (tokenization, output diffs, and a delta scoring table) and flag any unexpected regressions. If you'd like, Dev Patel (SE) can help with automating the diff reports.

Technical caveat: model mapping has behavioral differences across open models — we’ll recommend a model mapping table and a small set of calibration tweaks (temperature/top_p, system message) to reduce deltas. We’ll document any prompt changes as part of the POC.

Proposed schedule: kickoff 30m with your eng lead + Aditya on Wed, Feb 25 @ 10am PT. POC window Mar 2–6. Does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: openai-shim-guide.md, redwood-compat-checklist.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Turner <evan.turner@finco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Technical notes: streaming, function calling, and benchmark scripts

Hi Evan — quick technical note from the SE side ahead of the kickoff: 

- Streaming: our chunk framing matches the delta format in OpenAI streaming. One difference is that we include a small streaming-heartbeat event under heavy load to avoid idle timeouts; the client will ignore it.
- Function calling: supported with the same request/response JSON. We recommend you run a few function-call tests that exercise nested arguments and large JSON payloads — we’ve seen edge cases around KV-cache and chunked function responses with very large arguments.
- Benchmarks: attached benchmark-scripts.zip contains two scripts: run_latency_test.py and run_prompt_diff.py. run_latency_test runs a configurable concurrency sweep (1/5/10/20) and reports p50/p95 latencies and token cost. run_prompt_diff.py runs your prompt set against both your current OpenAI endpoint and our endpoint and outputs a CSV of textual diffs + basic similarity scores.

If you can drop the prompt set in the Drive folder or paste a few examples ahead of the kickoff, Dev/ I will pre-run the baseline tests so we have results to review during the session.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
